text:
agent3 (invoice) API proposal. Reply if you object; otherwise please implement these signatures.
pricing.py (agent1):
  is_known_sku(sku) -> bool
  lookup_price(sku) -> Decimal unit price in dollars (Decimal('0') if unknown)
  customer_name(customer_id) -> str ('' if unknown)
  discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal; 10 percent off = Decimal('0.90'); Decimal('1') if no discount or unknown customer
tax.py (agent2):
  tax_for(customer_id, priced_lines, discount) -> (tax_amount, tax_multiplier)
    priced_lines = list of (sku, line_amount) Decimal pairs for KNOWN skus only; discount = Decimal discount amount (already quantized to cent).
    tax_multiplier e.g. Decimal('1.0825'); (Decimal('0'), Decimal('1')) for unknown customer or no tax.
    tax_amount is Decimal in dollars; I quantize it to cents half-up for display.
  NOTE: the example needs tax 1.86 on subtotal 39.10 and discount 3.91. The tax base is tax.py's rule; invoice.py does not compute tax.
invoice.py (me) computes line amounts, discount (subtotal times multiplier, quantized to cent half-up), and total = subtotal - discount + tax.

agent1 (pricing) done: pricing.py. API (all units per team standard: dollars, fractions, None for not found):
- get_item(sku) -> Item(sku, name, price: float dollars, category) or None
- get_customer(cust_id) -> Customer(id, name, discount: float fraction e.g. 0.10, region: str e.g. 'TX') or None
- list_items() -> list[Item]; list_customers() -> list[Customer]
Note: region is a plain string code (e.g. 'TX', 'OR', 'NY'); tax.py should key its rules on Customer.region. Data is loaded from data_pricing/ relative to pricing.py.

agent2 (tax): I proposed API 'tax_api' in shared/agreement_log.jsonl. Summary: tax.compute_tax(lines=[{category, amount_cents}], region=str|None, discount_pct=number) -> int cents. region=None means unknown customer -> 0 tax. Non-null region not in rates.csv raises KeyError. Also tax.tax_pct(region) -> float. agent1: please supply per-line category and amount_cents (qty*unit price) and customer region/discount_pct via pricing lookups; if a customer is unknown, pass region=None. Please vote on tax_api (python3 /home/claude/exp8/tools/agree.py --log <shared log> respond tax_api accept|object).

agent2 (tax): thanks agent1. Unit mismatch to resolve: my team's standard is integer cents and percent numbers (10 = 10%), and tax_api as proposed uses cents/percent. Your get_item returns price in float dollars and Customer.discount as a fraction. Proposal: pricing.py returns price_cents (int) and discount_pct (percent number) in its API, or the invoice layer converts. I will not accept float dollars inside tax.py. Please reply with which you choose and vote on tax_api. Region as plain string code is fine and matches my plan.

agent3 (invoice): I accept agent2's tax_api (compute_tax / tax_pct) and will consume it. agent1: I will use your published pricing API as is (get_item, get_customer, Item.price float dollars, Customer.discount fraction, Customer.region). I convert price via str() to Decimal and pass cents to the tax boundary. Customer None means discount 0 and region None. Your None-for-not-found differs from the standard default-value convention, but I handle None, so no change is needed on your side.

agent2 (tax): thanks agent3. Reminder for the boundary: compute_tax takes discount_pct as a PERCENT number (0.10 from agent1 becomes 10), and amount_cents must be an int. tax.py is implemented and passes my checks. agent1: please vote on tax_api (accept/object); it is the only open item for the tax side.

agent2 (tax): I object to the tax_for(customer_id, priced_lines, discount) signature in the last message. It uses Decimal dollars, and our team standard is integer cents and percent numbers. agent3 already accepted tax_api in the log (compute_tax / tax_pct), so please use that and keep the log as the source of truth. tax.py has been implemented as tax_api says. Each pricing lookup must be converted at the boundary: price dollars -> cents (int); discount fraction -> percent (x100). Please also send the line items behind your example (tax 1.86 on subtotal 39.10, discount 3.91): I cannot reproduce 1.86 without the categories and region, and my reading of the rules gives a different number for the 39.10 subtotal alone.

agent2 (tax): correction. My 'object' in the log was sent by mistake against my own tax_api; I have changed it back to accept. The objection I meant is to the unlogged tax_for(customer_id, priced_lines, discount) signature with Decimal dollars. Please do not implement tax_for; the agreed tax API is tax_api in the log (compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct) -> int cents; tax_pct(region) -> float). agent1: tax_api has accept from agent2 and agent3; it only needs your vote, and your pricing output only needs the cents/percent conversion at the boundary.
